# Mechanical_calculator -- assembly notes

## Identity

A desk-scale hand-driven calculating machine: one heavy cast hull (the single root
part), a sloped or flat key bed carrying N independently sprung keys, a raised rear
register whose digits sit on rotating wheels or drums, one hand drive member on a
hull face, and a small bank of setting or clearing controls.  Exactly one root
part; every other part is a direct child of the hull; the only legal two-level
chain in the pool is `hull -> crank -> grip` (002 L443-L456, 003 L428-L441).  All
three origins assert the single-root/`len(joints) == len(parts) - 1` invariant
themselves (001 L517-L530, 002 L512-L524, 003 L450-L463).

## Domain arithmetic

core_domain = 5 housing_form x 5 register_assembly x 5 drive_member x 3 key_form
x 3 setting_control = 1125, every one of which must build -- `TemplateDomain` has
no compatibility gates.  raw_domain = 1125 x 11 N values (N in [6,16]) = 12,375.
Palette, continuous proportions, tick/mark counts and decorative density count
toward neither.  N is multiplicity and is excluded from core per AUTHORING
section 4.

## Domain reduction, and the VDM / section 4 justification for each decision

The first pass declared ten slots at 5*6*5*4*3*3*6*2*2 = 259,200 core combinations
and 41 baseline probes against a 120 s soft budget.  That is not a usable domain.
Six slots at 1125 core and 21 baseline probes is.  Every decision below applies the
`VISUAL_DIVERSITY_MODEL.md` test honestly -- does the candidate change the part
tree, the joint set, or the primary silhouette on its own?

- `calculator_topology` is NOT a slot.  Four of its five records are strictly local
  (a single mesh function, a single CAD function, or two extra visuals on a part
  that already exists) and leave the part tree IDENTICAL, so merging them into one
  five-member family would destroy legitimate combinations the sources plainly
  support -- a pinwheel hull with a stepped drum is buildable and historically
  correct.  The VDM merge rule triggers only when a candidate MUST change the whole
  host.  Each of the five therefore joins the slot that owns the subsystem it edits:
  pinwheel and lever-adder hulls -> housing_form; stepped drum -> register_assembly;
  rotary dial -> drive_member; comptometer cap -> key_form, and its slider deletion
  -> setting_control = none.
- The ONE real independence failure is the rotary dial.  As an independent slot,
  `rotary_dial x front_reciprocating_lever` would be unbuildable by local
  adaptation: the dial is a 0.100 m disc concentric with the drive pivot, and the
  front lever moves that pivot to (0.105, -0.247, 0.030), where a 0.058 m-radius
  disc would sweep 0.028 m below z=0 and through the key bed.  Relocating it is not
  a shoulder, a transition frame or an opening -- it is a different machine.  Per
  AUTHORING section 4 and MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 3 that is exactly the merge
  case, so `coaxial_rotary_dial` is a CANDIDATE OF drive_member sharing the one
  bearing-axis interface with the four crank/lever candidates.
- MERGED: register_bank_form (6) + register_wheel_form (4) + carry_mechanism (3)
  -> register_assembly (5).  Individually all thirteen pass the VDM test, so this
  is the AUTHORING section 4 merge rule, not a "they were only decoration" merge.
  The spin axis is set by the wheel, but the bank's window slots, divider planting
  and readout plane are DERIVED from that axis.  Pairing a face-on pinwheel with a
  mullion window row would run the window slot perpendicular to the digit face --
  the shell would have to be re-authored, not locally adapted.  The pool confirms
  the co-variance: no record mixes them; all 19 keep shell, wheel and carry train
  together.  Nothing is lost -- all six shells, all four wheel members and all
  three carry trains survive inside the five candidates.
- DEMOTED to continuous parameters: `wide_overhanging_carriage_tower` and
  `traveling_carriage_register`.  The record builds NO carriage -- no prismatic
  joint, no rails, no cavity, only a Box resize -- and a pure proportion change is
  not a candidate.  It becomes register_tower_width/depth/height.  A real traveling
  carriage would have reparented all N register wheels onto a moving carriage: a
  part-tree change with no source attestation, on the axis where the budget is
  tightest.  Rejected; its mechanical template is recorded in the SourceMap.
- DEMOTED to slot-local discrete parameters: `has_paper_transport` in {0,1} and
  `function_key_count` in {0,6}, both on `tapered_wedge` only (the only lineage
  that prints and the only one with a function block).  A two-member slot doubles
  the whole cartesian product to buy one optional assembly appearing in 1 of 19
  records; the function keys are the SAME mechanism as the key matrix.
- COLLAPSED 3 -> 1: the three slider banks, into `slider_bank` with
  `slider_count` in {2,3,4}, adopting 003's paired-rail 3-piece construction
  (the only section 6-conformant one).
- REJECTED: `carriage_reset_lever` adds no part and no joint; its crank-arm and
  mechanism-floor resizes survive as continuous parameters.

## Cross-slot risks, and how DERIVATION (never gating) resolves each

1. Deck tilt.  `open_frame_side_cheek` is flat (003, DECK_PITCH = 0) while the
   001 lineage is 0.271 rad and 002 is 0.218.  Every key joint, every slider joint
   and the deck plane interface are expressed in the DECK-TILTED frame, so a key
   candidate never learns which hull it is on: `deck_to_key_seating` derives the
   origin and `rpy=(deck_tilt,0,0)` from one plane interface that carries the real
   tilt.  The plane's `extent` is the real key-bed rectangle, never the hull AABB.
2. Register spin axis.  Three candidates spin about (1,0,0) and are read edge-on;
   two spin about (0,1,0) and are read face-on.  The readout plane, the divider
   planting and the tower stand-off are all derived from the candidate's own axis,
   which is why bank and wheel are ONE candidate and why the category anchors are
   scoped per family instead of asserting one axis for all five.
3. Drive face.  The pivot always sits ON a hull face at that face's local
   mid-height (001 z=0.190 = REAR_DECK_Z + rear-cover rise; 002 z=0.095 = mid of a
   0.014..0.153 profile; 003 z=0.135 = mid of a 0.055..0.195 cheek; front-lever
   z=0.030 = mid of a 0.055 fascia).  `hull_face_to_drive_bearing` derives WHICH
   face is bored and how large a clear disc that face must carry, so the dial's
   0.116 m backplate and the front lever's re-derived front lip are host
   adaptations, not excluded combinations.
4. Setting control on a tilted deck.  003's slider seat is derived ALONG THE DECK
   NORMAL (001 L344-L351: `y - sin(pitch)*0.00125`, `z + 0.0008 +
   cos(pitch)*0.00125`), never authored twice, so the same carriage seats correctly
   on a flat bed and on a 0.271 rad wedge.  The zeroing knob mounts on the register
   cover, whose real bearing rectangle is published as `PlaneInterface.extent`: the
   knob is 0.044 wide at x=0.145 on a cover reaching x=0.175, an 8 mm edge margin,
   so a wider knob or narrower tower must be rejected by `mate_planes` rather than
   hidden by a generous hull AABB.
5. Part budget.  See "## Multiplicity"; enforced by derivation in `resolve_config`.

## Collision budget, and the welding deviation

`sdk/_core/v0/exact_collisions.py::_generate_part_collisions` (L94-L104) loops
`for visual in part.visuals` and derives one collision solid per visual, 1:1, and
collision is computed only BETWEEN parts.  MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 1c makes
intra-part embedding free, so the rebuild WELDS each key and each register wheel
into a single solid instead of emitting three or eleven visuals apiece.  The
`stepped_drum_bank` candidate attests the route: the source fork unions eleven
features (drum, hub, nine teeth) into ONE solid at L54-L82.  Without the deviation
the worst case would emit ~120 collision solids; with it, ~68.

A second, larger deviation is stated rather than hidden: 001's EIGHT independently
articulated carry wheels (8 parts + 8 REVOLUTE joints, L403-L441) become ONE rack
part with ONE joint carrying all 24 visuals, following the construction 002 already
uses for the same function (`shifting_carry_rack`, L387-L414).  001's own author
tests never check their motion, only their joint limits (L579-L598).  This changes
HOW the carry train is emitted, not what it looks like, and it is what buys the N
range.

## The nine allow_overlap sites, and the bore correction that removes all of them

`ctx.allow_overlap` is BLOCKED for Design-backed templates (AUTHORING section 5,
`agent/prompts/sections/sdk_base.md`), including calls made through helpers or
aliases.  Seven of the 19 records emit allowances; none appear in 001 or 003.  All
nine sites reduce to two root causes, and both are cross-part FITS that a
0.3-1.0 mm bore correction removes with no visible change:

- Cause A (10 sites, 002 L599-L608 and inherited by five forks): drum bore
  r = 0.0021 against a common axle r = 0.0022 -- a 0.1 mm interference.  Fix:
  `drum_bore_r = axle_r + 0.0004` (binding register_shaft_to_wheel_bore).  The
  record's existing `expect_contact(contact_tol=0.0002)` at L627-L634 still passes,
  because the tangency comes from the hub shoulder, not from the bore.
- Cause B (2 sites: folding fork L689-L698, drive journal r=0.0045 against a
  torus hole r=0.004; front-lever fork L686-L695, an 0.011 shaft buried 0.007 m
  inside a SOLID 0.026 boss): fix by making the bearing a real ANNULUS with
  `bore_r = shaft_r + 0.0005..0.001` and letting the shaft's inner end plane
  coincide with the hull face.  A third grip site (002 L669-L677, the 0.018 capsule
  swallowing the 0.008 tube end) is fixed by giving the crank a real end pin and the
  grip a matching bore with 0.0005 radial clearance plus a thin shoulder washer that
  provides the tangent face contact.

`ctx.allow_isolated_part(...)` is NOT blocked and remains available for a
joint-retained member that is intentionally disconnected by a running clearance.

## The key-aperture correction -- the one place the rebuild must exceed the source

NO SOURCE RECORD CUTS A KEY APERTURE.  001 presses a 0.015 x 0.015 stem 0.006 m
into a solid hull deck; 002 presses a 0.006 square stem 0.004 m into a 0.004
`key_plate`; 003 presses a 0.010 stem 0.007 m into a 0.018 `keyboard_bed`; the
comptometer fork presses 0.009 m into the same solid bed.  Static poses look fine,
which is exactly the failure mode MECHANICAL_PRIORS sections 1 and 7 warn about,
and motion QC exercises the `upper` bound of every bounded prismatic joint.

RULE for the rebuild, derived from the moving member's envelope and never from a
magic number: cut a real aperture per key at the joint origin,
`aperture = stem_size + 2 * 0.0005` (002's 0.006 square becomes 0.007; 003's 0.010
round becomes 0.011), with depth >= `key_travel`.  The whole matrix is cut into the
deck skin as ONE `ExtrudeWithHolesGeometry` operation so the skin stays one visual,
and the skin is carried on a real perimeter well of depth `key_travel + 0.006` so
the stem descends into a genuine cavity rather than into cast metal.

The seating contact is then re-derived, because with a real aperture the source's
"stem base plane exactly on the deck top" no longer produces contact: the stem is
inside the hole.  The key instead carries a RETAINER FLANGE under the skin -- the
real mechanical feature that stops a sprung key from leaving its bore -- whose top
face overlaps the skin underside by 0.0002 m at rest.  That is a deliberate
part-to-part overlap sized against `find_geometry_overlaps`'s 1e-3 tolerance and
not the 5 mm environment default (MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 1c: exact tangency
between two parts is fragile because CadQuery may keep tangent solids separate and
triangulation may open the seam).  On the press stroke the flange moves DOWN, away
from the skin and into the well, so the contact exists at rest and the interference
never does.  `expect_contact(key, hull, contact_tol=1e-4)` -- 002 L580-L595 asserts
0.0002 and 003 L590-L595 asserts 1e-5 -- still passes.

## The rest of the mating rules, all derivations

- `key_joint_origin_z = deck_top_face_z` (001: `_deck_z(y)`; 002: `DECK_SURFACE_Z
  + local_y*sin(tilt)`; 003: 0.081 = keyboard_bed top).  Every key's lowest visual
  has its base plane at local z = 0.
- `divider_width = wheel_pitch - drum_axial_length - 2 * 0.0005`, dividers planted
  at the wheel midpoints with D+1 of them (001 L150-L153).  For the face-on bank the
  equivalent is `tooth_envelope_diameter <= wheel_pitch - 0.002`.
- Reading clearance stays a REAL GAP: 0.0005 m of air between the printed digit and
  the pane (001 L164, L382-L387), and 003 stacks card 0.1645 / glass 0.1640 / bezel
  0.163 in 1.5 mm steps.
- `tower_front_y = wheel_shaft_far_end + 0.005` -- the one number the register
  forks assert (`expect_gap(register_tower, wheel_shaft, axis='y', 0.004..0.006)`,
  exposed-pinwheel fork L565-L573).
- `rail_clear_span = carriage_width + 2 * 0.0005`.  003's exact-fit 0.014 span on a
  0.014 carriage is a zero-distance contact that reads as a collision, so it is
  opened to 0.015.  `rail_length >= travel + carriage_depth + 0.020`.
- Effort/velocity envelope across the pool: keys 3.0-8.0 at 0.09-0.10; function
  keys 12.0; sliders 4.0-10.0; carry rack 8.0 at 0.05; counter wheels 0.6-2.0 at
  6.0-8.0; cranks 15.0-25.0 at 3.0-5.0; the two hand levers 35.0 at 1.8-2.5; grips
  0.4-1.5.  The drive member always carries the largest effort in the model.

## Corrections made while implementing, recorded rather than hidden

- `ExtrudeWithHolesGeometry` keeps its hole profiles as inner WALLS, not voids, so
  the key aperture is built from an explicit annular prism (matching outer and
  hole rings joined by annular caps).  A square aperture samples its corners, and
  a round one is inflated to the circumscribing polygon, so the modelled 0.5 mm
  clearance is the real one and not a polygon artefact.
- The column law also reads the cap: a plunger cap over 0.024 m cannot make ten
  columns fit a 0.35-0.40 m hull, so that family runs the 003 lineage's five
  columns at 0.055 x 0.045 (003 L21-L22, L248-L250).  Pitch opens up for a larger
  cap before the deck clamps it, which is what the pool actually shows (0.015 cap
  at a 0.020 pitch in 002, 0.034 at 0.055 in 003).
- The selector lane sits BEHIND the key field, as 003 builds it (sliders at
  y = +0.020 against keys at -0.155..-0.020), not beside it; the deck reserves
  that strip so a five-column field and a slider bank both fit.
- `find_geometry_overlaps` prefilters on the per-visual AABB intersection and only
  calls FCL when it exceeds `overlap_tol` on all three axes.  A deliberate contact
  is therefore made by overlapping two SMALL elements by 0.2 mm along one axis
  (crank hub to bearing collar, wheel hub to divider, carriage flange to rail
  tops).  Where the counterpart is a large panel -- key to deck skin, grip to
  crank pin, face-on wheel to shaft rail, paper roll to its standards -- the fit
  stays a REAL running clearance and the member is declared with
  `ctx.allow_isolated_part`, which sdk_base.md keeps available for a joint-retained
  part disconnected by clearance.  No `allow_overlap` is emitted anywhere.

## Multiplicity -- key_matrix (N over key_form)

`key_matrix` is multiplicity, not a component slot.  `design-init` scaffolds it as
a two-candidate slot (`keypad_layout` / `matrix_layout`), which would fold N into
`core_domain` and assert 2250 core combinations.  That is wrong twice over:
AUTHORING section 4 excludes N from core, and the two "candidates" are two
PLACEMENT LAWS for one mechanism, selected by N itself, not two components.  The
slot is dropped here and re-declared as a multiplicity whose `item_slot` is
`key_form`, giving core = 5 x 5 x 5 x 3 x 3 = 1125.

### The exact index-general rule, preserved verbatim

Both 002-lineage forks converge on the same code (50-key L296-L329; 90-key
L296-L331):

    KEY_COLUMNS = 10                       # constant in 002, 50-key and 90-key
    KEY_ROWS    = ceil(N / KEY_COLUMNS)
    row, column = divmod(key_index, KEY_COLUMNS)          # flat index
    local_x = (column - (KEY_COLUMNS - 1) / 2) * pitch_x
    local_y = (row    - (KEY_ROWS    - 1) / 2) * pitch_y  # matrix centred on deck
    world_y = DECK_CENTER_Y  + local_y * cos(DECK_TILT)
    world_z = DECK_SURFACE_Z + local_y * sin(DECK_TILT)
    joint origin = Origin(xyz=(local_x, world_y, world_z), rpy=(DECK_TILT, 0, 0))
    axis         = (0, 0, -1);  limits 0 -> key_travel
    part  name   = f"key_{row}_{column}"
    joint name   = f"key_{row}_{column}_press"
    parent       = housing                 # flat, never chained key-to-key

Pitch derivation, unifying both source endpoints:
`plate_depth = KEY_ROWS * pitch_y + 0.014` and `cover_depth = KEY_ROWS * pitch_y
+ 0.038` (50-key fork L165-L191: 8 rows -> 0.198/0.174, 5 rows -> 0.138/0.114),
then `pitch_y = min(0.020, (plate_depth_max - cap_y - 2 * 0.005) / (KEY_ROWS - 1))`
(90-key fork L299: 9 rows at 0.020 would span 8*0.020 + cap 0.015 = 0.175 against a
0.174 plate, a 1 mm overflow, so the pitch drops to 0.0185 and the deck is left
untouched).  Ragged last row: when N is not a multiple of the column count the last
row is centred on its own occupancy, `local_x = (column - (row_occupancy - 1)/2) *
pitch_x`.  No source sample is ragged (10, 20, 50, 80, 81, 90 are all exact), so
this changes nothing the pool attests.

### The layout switch, which is a DERIVATION of N and not a slot

- `N <= 12` -> keypad_layout: 3 columns, pitch (0.050, 0.043), cap 0.028 x 0.026,
  remainder centred on the last row.  Source 10-key fork L76-L101 and L247-L282
  builds 1..9 as a 3x3 field with the zero centred below (`row = i//3, column =
  i%3` for `i < 9`, then `row = 3, column = 1`), and its keys are physically
  larger than 002's 0.015 squares.
- `N > 12` -> matrix_layout: 10 columns for the 001/002 lineages, 5 columns at
  pitch 0.055 x 0.045 for the 003 lineage, pitch and cap per the rule above.

### Range: N in [6, 16]

LOWER BOUND 6 -- GEOMETRY, not provenance.  The SourceMap's first pass proposed
10 on the grounds that it is "the smallest sample in the pool and a real machine".
That is provenance, and AUTHORING section 3 says explicitly that source integers
are evidence the rule holds, never the bound.  Re-examined, the real floor is the
placement law plus legibility: the pitch derivation contains `(KEY_ROWS - 1)` in a
denominator, so `KEY_ROWS >= 2` is a hard requirement of the law itself, and the
category anchor requires a key MATRIX rather than a row of buttons.  Under the
keypad law's 3 columns, two full rows is N = 6.  So 6 is where the mechanism stops
being general, and it is lowered from 10 deliberately: the 3x3-plus-centred-zero
keypad at N = 10 stays reachable and stays the source-attested configuration, but
it is not the floor.  N = 6, 7, 8, 9 are ordinary ragged-last-row fields under the
same rule.

UPPER BOUND 16 -- HOST CAPACITY AND MEASURED BUDGET, and it is a cap, said plainly.
Parsing 452 cached preflight reports under `.cache/template_check/*/preflight/*.json`,
the largest object this fleet has ever shipped is 33 parts / 32 joints
(`shelving_unit_with_adjustable_shelves`), second 25/24
(`pictureX_0611_flexible_track_lighting_system`), fleet p90 19 parts, median 8.5.
Cost is `builds x per-build cost`, not part count alone: `wrench_set` at 12 parts
already burns 128.5 s against a 120 s soft budget inside a 150 s watchdog, and the
largest observed probe count is ~103 (`studio_lamp`).  Worst host after the domain
reduction is `1 hull + 11 register + 2 crank&grip + 4 sliders = 18` parts, so
N = 16 lands at 34 parts / 33 joints -- AT the measured ceiling, not past it.  Best
host is 9, so N = 6 lands at 15 parts, just under the fleet p90.  Mandatory
motion-QC poses at N = 16 worst host are ~66, comparable to the shelving unit the
fleet already runs.

HOST CAPACITY is enforced by DERIVATION in `resolve_config`, never by removing a
combination (AUTHORING section 6 forbids the latter): `granted_function_keys` and
`granted_paper_roll` are admitted only while `host_parts + N + extra <= 33`.  Both
optional dressings keep an unconditional geometric effect (the deck's six function
apertures and sill; the hull's carry bed, bridge, posts and paper standards, which
source 001 L169-L194 builds as hull visuals anyway), so the discrete parameters
still respond even when the rotating part is not granted.

WHAT IS GIVEN UP, stated plainly.  The source's 20-, 50-, 80-, 81- and 90-key
records are OUTSIDE the declared domain -- five of the six N samples in the pool
cannot be reproduced at full count.  The rebuild is a mechanically faithful
calculator whose key field is smaller than four of the six sources.  That is a real
loss of source fidelity, accepted deliberately, because an aspirational N = 90
(106-120 parts, 336-494 collision solids, 3.2-3.6x anything this fleet has built)
makes `corner` unrunnable.  The index-general rule above is preserved verbatim and
is correct for any N, so raising the cap later is a one-line domain change.

NO FAKING.  Every key in the declared range is a real independently articulated
part with its own PRISMATIC joint and its own aperture in the deck.  Nothing is
welded into the deck to inflate a count, and no token subset is articulated in
front of a static painted-on remainder.

derived.name: deck_top_face_z_m
derived.rationale: THE central derivation of the category: key_joint_origin_z = deck_top_face_z. 001 L255 uses _deck_z(y) directly; 002 L305-L306 uses DECK_SURFACE_Z + local_y*sin(tilt); 003 L280 uses 0.081, which is exactly the keyboard_bed's top face (0.072 + 0.018/2). The rebuild adds the well and skin the sources do not have, so the deck top face is derived from the hull seat plus both, never authored twice.

derived.name: deck_skin_thickness_m
derived.rationale: Thickness of the perforated key plate. Must be at least the travel so a through-cut aperture is by construction >= key_travel deep (section 7).

derived.name: key_well_depth_m
derived.rationale: Depth of the real cavity under the skin, so the stem and the retainer flange descend into air rather than into cast metal. The well perimeter rim embeds 0.002 m into the hull (intra-part, free per section 1c).

derived.name: key_aperture_size_m
derived.rationale: MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 7: the opening is derived from the moving member's envelope plus a safety clearance, never from a fixed magic number. 002's 0.006 square stem gives a 0.007 aperture; 003's 0.010 round stem gives 0.011. NO source record cuts this opening at all.

derived.name: key_retainer_size_m
derived.rationale: Retainer flange across the underside of the skin -- the feature that stops a sprung key from leaving its bore, and the rebuild's replacement for the source's stem-on-solid-plate seating.

derived.name: key_seating_overlap_m
derived.rationale: Deliberate part-to-part overlap of the flange top into the skin underside at rest. Sized against find_geometry_overlaps's overlap_tol of 1e-3, not the 5 mm environment default; section 1c says exact tangency between two parts is fragile. It disappears on the press stroke because the flange travels away from the skin.

derived.name: key_press_effort
derived.rationale: Pool effort envelope for key presses is 3.0 (002 L318) to 8.0 (001 L262, 003 L283), velocity 0.09-0.10.

derived.expression: 3 if key_matrix <= 12 else (5 if housing_form == 'open_frame_side_cheek' else 10)
derived.name: key_matrix_columns
derived.rationale: The keypad/matrix switch is a DERIVATION OF N, not a slot. N<=12 is the 10-key fork's 3-column pad (L247-L282); N>12 is the 002-lineage 10-column rule (L296-L329) or the 003 lineage's 5 columns (003 L22).

derived.name: key_rows
derived.rationale: KEY_ROWS = ceil(N / KEY_COLUMNS), verbatim from 002-lineage L296-L331.

derived.expression: 0.050 if key_matrix <= 12 else (0.055 if housing_form == 'open_frame_side_cheek' else 0.020)
derived.name: key_pitch_x_m
derived.rationale: Pitch in X: 0.020 in 002, the 50-key fork and the 90-key fork alike -- constant, never re-derived; 0.055 in 003 (L250); 0.050 in the 10-key pad (L257).

derived.name: key_plate_depth_max_m
derived.rationale: How much of the hull depth the key bed may claim before it collides with the register shoulder. 002: plate 0.174 on a 0.340 hull = 0.512.

derived.name: key_pitch_y_m
derived.rationale: THE unified pitch rule, reproducing BOTH source endpoints exactly. The 50-key fork shrinks the DECK to fit the matrix (L165-L191: cover 0.252x0.198 -> 0.252x0.138, plate 0.222x0.174 -> 0.222x0.114); the 90-key fork leaves the deck untouched and shrinks the PITCH instead (L299: 0.020 -> 0.0185, because 9 rows at 0.020 span 8*0.020 + cap 0.015 = 0.175 against a 0.174 plate, a 1 mm overflow). Derive the plate from the matrix, then clamp the pitch.

derived.expression: 0.043 if key_matrix <= 12 else (0.045 if housing_form == 'open_frame_side_cheek' else 0.020)
derived.name: key_pitch_y_nominal_m
derived.rationale: Nominal Y pitch before clamping: 0.043 (10-key pad L258), 0.045 (003 L248), 0.020 (002 L274).

derived.name: key_plate_depth_m
derived.rationale: 50-key fork L165-L191, verified against both its own 5-row and its parent's 8-row geometry: 8 rows -> 0.174, 5 rows -> 0.114.

derived.name: key_cover_depth_m
derived.rationale: The same fork's outer cover: 8 rows -> 0.198, 5 rows -> 0.138.

derived.name: key_plate_width_m
derived.rationale: 002: 10 columns at 0.020 give a 0.222 plate, i.e. a 0.0135 first-key inset per side against a 0.195 field span.

derived.name: key_cap_clearance_m
derived.rationale: Neighbour gap. RULE: cap <= 0.75 * min(pitch), keeping the caps apart. The 90-key fork is the tightest case in the pool at 0.0035 m (0.81 ratio) and sets the practical floor.

derived.name: host_part_count
derived.rationale: Everything except the key matrix and the two optional dressings. Worst host is 18 (railed_drum_bank at 11 + crank and grip + 4 sliders), best is 9.

derived.expression: function_key_count if host_part_count + key_matrix + function_key_count <= 33 else 0
derived.name: granted_function_keys

derived.rationale: THE fix for cause A of the pool's allow_overlap sites. Source 002 builds bore 0.0021 against axle 0.0022 -- a 0.1 mm interference and the direct cause of ten allowances at L599-L608. RULE: drum_bore_r = axle_r + 0.0003..0.0005, never <= axle_r.

derived.name: drum_axial_length_m
derived.rationale: Pool: pitch 0.022 with a 0.014 drum (001), pitch 0.021 with 0.016 + 0.002 hub (002). Derived from the pitch so the divider rule below closes.

derived.name: divider_width_m
derived.rationale: The pool's register clearance rule, measured across all three origins: 001 pitch 0.022 - drum 0.014 - 2*0.001 = 0.006 mullion (L150-L153); 002 pitch 0.021 - drum 0.018 - 2*0.0005 = 0.002 divider (L207-L214). D+1 dividers are planted at the wheel midpoints plus both ends.

derived.name: wheel_hub_overlap_m
derived.rationale: The wheel's hub is 2*(0.0005 + 0.0002) longer than the drum so it overlaps each neighbouring divider by 0.2 mm: a deliberate, rotationally symmetric part-to-part contact that survives every pose. 001 attests the construction -- its 0.017 hub protrudes 1.5 mm each side of a 0.014 drum as a real journal (L371-L381).

derived.name: register_part_count
derived.rationale: D wheels plus one carry rack for the counter-drum family (the face-on family's carry rack is static hull geometry in 003 L204-L216). This is where 001's eight independently articulated carry wheels become one rack part -- the deviation that buys the N range.

derived.name: wheel_shaft_far_end_y_m
derived.rationale: Front end of the face-on wheel shaft. 003: shaft 0.130 long about y=0.095 ends at 0.160.

derived.name: tower_front_y_m
derived.rationale: THE one stand-off the register forks actually assert: exposed-pinwheel fork L565-L573 requires expect_gap(register_tower, wheel_shaft, axis='y', 0.004..0.006), and 003's geometry gives exactly 0.165 - 0.160 = 0.005.

derived.expression: tower_front_y_m - 0.0005 if register_spin_axis == '(0,1,0)' else register_center_y_m - drum_radius_m - 0.0025
derived.name: readout_face_y_m
derived.rationale: The readout plane. Face-on: card 0.1645 / glass 0.1640 / bezel 0.163 in 1.5 mm steps (003 L174-L194). derived.name: readout_extent_x_m
derived.rationale: Real readout width, published as PlaneInterface.extent instead of the hull AABB.

derived.name: readout_extent_z_m
derived.rationale: Real readout height. 001: a 0.034-high pane against a 0.032 drum.

derived.name: register_center_z_m
derived.rationale: The register sits above the rear of the deck: 001 z=0.176 above REAR_DECK_Z 0.155; 002 z=0.165; 003 z=0.155.

derived.expression: '(0,1,0)' if drive_member == 'front_reciprocating_lever' else ('(-1,0,0)' if drive_member == 'vertical_pull_lever' else '(1,0,0)')
derived.name: drive_face_normal
derived.rationale: The joint axis IS the outward normal of the hull face the bearing is bored into. Flank (1,0,0) for 001/002/003 and the dial; front wall (0,1,0) for the front lever (fork L515-L520); (-1,0,0) for the one-way pull lever (fork L508-L514).

derived.expression: (hull_width_m * 0.5, drive_pivot_y_m, drive_face_mid_height_m) if drive_face_normal == '(1,0,0)' else (0.28 * hull_width_m, -hull_depth_m * 0.5, drive_face_mid_height_m)
derived.name: drive_pivot_xyz_m
derived.rationale: The pivot always sits ON a hull face, never inset and never floating. 003 L396 puts it at x=0.190, exactly the side-cheek outer face; the front-lever fork at y=-0.247, on the front wall.

derived.name: drive_face_mid_height_m
derived.rationale: RULE: the pivot is at the local MID-HEIGHT of the face it is bored into, derived and never authored twice. 001 z=0.190 = REAR_DECK_Z 0.155 + the 0.035 rear-cover rise; 002 z=0.095 = mid of the 0.014..0.153 side profile; 003 z=0.135 = mid of the 0.055..0.195 cheek; the front-lever fork z=0.030 = mid of the 0.055-high fascia.

derived.name: drive_bore_radius_m
derived.rationale: THE fix for cause B. The bearing must be an ANNULUS with bore_r = shaft_r + 0.0005..0.001. The folding fork runs a 0.0045 journal in a 0.004 torus hole (0.5 mm interference, allow_overlap at L689-L698) and the front-lever fork buries an 0.011 shaft 0.007 m inside a SOLID 0.026 boss (allow_overlap at L686-L695). Both disappear under this rule with no change to the visible form.

derived.name: drive_thrust_overlap_m
derived.rationale: The crank hub bears against the bearing's outer face with a deliberate 0.2 mm overlap -- rotationally symmetric, so the contact holds at every pose. This is what replaces the source's butt contact (003 L396: shaft local x0 = 0 exactly on the cheek face, asserted expect_contact(1e-5) at L602-L607) now that the bore is a real clearance.

derived.name: grip_pin_radius_m
derived.rationale: The crank's end pin. The grip's bore is pin_r + 0.0005, and a thin shoulder washer provides the tangent face contact -- the SourceMap's fix for 002 L669-L677, where an 0.018 capsule simply swallowed the 0.008 tube end.

derived.name: grip_axis_local
derived.rationale: The grip stub axis is parallel to the pivot axis for the crank candidates. The folding crank is the exception and the whole point of that candidate: its grip hinges about (0,1,0) from 0 to 84 degrees instead of spinning freely (fork L466-L483).

derived.name: drive_sweep_radius_m
derived.rationale: The member's entire swept circle must lie outside the hull footprint. 001 satisfies this by placing the pivot 0.056 m behind the rear wall; 003 by placing it exactly on the cheek face so the whole 0.075 circle is outboard of x = 0.190.

derived.name: drive_clear_disc_radius_m
derived.rationale: HOST ADAPTATION: how large a flat clear disc the bored face must carry. The dial candidate grows a 0.116 backplate, a TorusGeometry(0.052, 0.0018) scale ring and ten index marks on that face (fork L292-L327); the crank candidates need only the bearing boss.

derived.name: drive_part_count
derived.rationale: A second REVOLUTE grip child is optional but, when present, its origin equals the crank's handle point exactly.

derived.name: drive_effort
derived.rationale: The drive member always carries the largest effort in the model. Cranks 15.0-25.0 at velocity 3.0-5.0; the two hand levers 35.0 at 1.8-2.5.

derived.name: setting_seat_z_m
derived.rationale: The slider bank seats on the key deck (003 L356: joint origin z=0.081 = keyboard-bed top); the zeroing knob seats on the register cover (fork L360: origin z=0.240, and tower_cover Box(0.350,0.060,0.030) at z=0.225 has its top face at exactly 0.240).

derived.name: setting_seat_y_m
derived.rationale: The control lane sits just behind the key field, derived from the field the matrix actually occupies rather than from a fixed y.

derived.name: slider_carriage_width_m
derived.rationale: 003 L334: Box((0.014, 0.012, 0.006)) carriage, plus a 0.0045 x 0.022 stem and a 0.014 x 0.010 x 0.012 grip -- a genuine 3-piece member, not a tab.

derived.name: slider_rail_clear_span_m
derived.rationale: MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 6. 003's rails at x +- 0.009 leave an exact 0.014 clear span on a 0.014 carriage -- a zero-distance contact that will read as a collision, so the rebuild opens it to 0.015.

derived.name: slider_rail_length_m
derived.rationale: RULE: rail_length >= travel + carriage_depth + 0.020. 003 builds 0.060 rails for a 0.028 stroke on a 0.012-deep carriage.

derived.name: slider_seat_offset_xyz_m
derived.rationale: The seat is derived ALONG THE DECK NORMAL, verbatim from 001 L344-L351, which is what makes one slider construction work on a flat bed and on a 0.271 rad wedge alike.

derived.name: setting_seat_width_m
derived.rationale: REAL bearing rectangle for PlaneInterface.extent. The zeroing knob is 0.044 wide at x=0.145 on a cover that only reaches x=0.175 -- an 8 mm edge margin. A wider knob, a narrower tower or a more outboard x and the knob half-overhangs, which mate_planes must reject rather than the hull AABB hide (MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 2).

derived.name: setting_seat_depth_m
derived.rationale: Same rectangle, in the other tangent direction.

derived.name: setting_seat_overlap_m
derived.rationale: The carriage underside and the knob base each embed 0.2 mm into their seat. The knob is rotationally symmetric and the carriage slides in-plane, so the contact holds at every pose.

derived.expression: slider_count if setting_control == 'slider_bank' else (1 if setting_control == 'zeroing_knob' else 0)
